messages.subject: Re: new error appearing using matR
messages.body_plain:
That message usually means you are trying to access private data without a valid token.

Make sure that your account has access to the metagenomes, and follow the posting for
accessing private data if you have not done so before.

Note that tokens expire after a number of months.

Cheers
Kevin

messages.subject: Getting metadata, latitude|longitude from matR
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I have been using a R script using (matR) to get latitude and longitude data for lists of MG-RAST id's. The MGRAST metaserver was down today and now it is back up and I can't get the script to work. I can download the biom files, but the second step is not converting the file and the third step is not getting the latitude/longitude metadata.

library (matR)
#1
mbnA <- biomRequest ("mgm4447016.3, mgm4447020.3, mgm4447101.3, mgm4461363.3, mgm4461364.3, mgm4461365.3, mgm4461366.3, mgm4461367.3, mgm4461368.3, mgm4472090.3, mgm4472091.3, mgm4472094.3, mgm4472095.3, mgm4472096.3, mgm4472098.3, mgm4472100.3, mgm4472102.3, mgm4472105.3, mgm4472138.3, mgm4472139.3, mgm4472140.3, mgm4472142.3, mgm4472162.3, mgm4472164.3, mgm4472171.3", request="function")
#2
mbnA1 <- transform (mbnA, t_Threshold, t_Log)
#3
mbnA2 <- columns (mbnA1, "latitude|longitude")

Do you have any thoughts of what might be going wrong now? Thanks.

Sincerely, Michaeline

messages.subject: Analyzing HMP data with matR - a small-scale example
messages.subject_clean: Analyzing HMP data with matR - a small-scale example
messages.body_plain:
# A few notes before we start:
# adapted from an earlier version of this example - HMP_example.9-4-14.R
# Lines that start with a pound (#), like this one, are commented out, and will not run
# All other lines (like the one below) contain R code that can be run
# If you are using R studio, you can run through this example by cut/pasting lines into the console(below),
# or clicking on the run button (upper right).
# If you are using R outside of R studio, simply cut and paste the code into the R console.

# Notes before we start:
# - I use R studio when I can, but have found that it frequently crashes/ hangs unexpectedly.
#     if this happens, I would recommend using the GUI version of R, or R from the terminal
# - Users frequently use Excel to open data files and perform manipulations by hand.
#     As long as you keep the file in the same format as a tab-delimited text, you
#     won't have any problems on PC/Windows, but will run into problems with OSX

# We'll cover retreival of mgrast ids and metadata in another example.
# Here we focus on
#      - getting annotation abundance data from MG-RAST
#      - processing the annotation data (remove singletons, normalize the data)
#      - producing visualizations that use both the annotation abundance data
#        and the sample metadata
#             -- PCoA (single or in batch mode)
#             -- Heatmap dendrogram
#      - performing statistical analyse on the data (single or in batch mode)

# In addition to the data that you will download, this example requires two
# additional files:
#     hmp_metadata.txt # this file contains appropriately formatted metadata for the samples
#     hmp.IDs                # this file contains a list of mg-rast ids for the samples

# say hello
print("Hello World")

# make sure you are in the directory that contains these two files
# hmp.IDs
# hmp_metadata.txt

## CHECK YOUR R VERSION -- has to be 2.15 or newer
R.Version()

## INSTALL PACKAGED
# This example requires two packages (devtools & matR) - here we install them:
install.packages("devtools")
library(devtools)
install_github("MG-RAST/matR")
library(matR)
dependencies()
source("http://bioconductor.org/biocLite.R")
biocLite("preprocessCore")

## DOWNLOAD DATA (to read data from hmp.Rda, skip to the next section)
# Vadim I commented out the taxonomic view so you can see what a taxonomic call would look like
# at the end of the example I show how to do something a little fuancier - download multiple
# functional levels at the same time -- for now we'll stick with level 3

## HOW TO GET A KEY FOR ACCESSING YOUR PRIVATE DATA
## No key is needed to access public data in MG-RAST
## For private data, get your MG-RAST key and use the the msessesion$setAuth() function
## You will find more detailed instructions on obtaining and using your key here:
## https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/matr-forum/R1anCspxiHs

## LOAD SAMPLE IDS
## load ids from a list (your mgids should be in a single column
## a single column excel "saved as" tab delimited text will work fine
## An example file would look something like this (without the #'s and spaces )
#     mgm4472580.3
#     mgm472896.3
#     mgm472575.3
#     mgm472631.3
# Now you can read in your ids
my_ids <- readIDs(file="hmp.IDs")
# make sure that the IDs have the "mgm" prefix
# I have attached this list of samples to this email

## DEFINE VIEW(S) FOR DATA DOWNLOAD
# At the same time we will download functional and taxonomic data for the same dataset
# This is possible for (most) WGS data; only taxonomic data are available for annotated
# 16s amplicon sequences
# first a view for level 3 subsystem functional annotations, then a view for genus level
# taxonomic annotations
my_views <- list(
  ss_l3_counts=c(entry="counts", annot="function", level="level3", source="Subsystems"),
  taxa_genus_counts=c(entry="counts", annot="organism", level="genus", source="M5RNA")
)

## DOWNLOAD DATA FOR SELECTED SAMPLES AND VIEW(S)
# we download the data into a matR "collection"
# A "collection is an object that can contain abundance counts for multiple views
# It is a convenient way to handle data when you want to examine it at several levels
# and keep everything together
hmp_collection <- collection(my_ids, my_views)
# NOTE: Depending on the server response time, this step will take several seconds
# to several minutes. When you see the following text:
#      request posted: counts : function : level3 : Subsystems : na
#      request posted: counts : organism : genus : M5RNA : all
# it means that the request has been successfully submitted, but the data may not my
# downloaded yet. To see if the data are downloaded, try to view them:
hmp_collection$ss_l3_counts
# OR
hmp_collection$taxa_genus_counts
# If you get a message like this one:
#      data is pending
#      [,1]
#      [1,] "24241"
# It means that the API is still processing your request
# wait a few minutes and check again
# When you see a table of annotations and numbers, you know that your
# data have downloaded, and can proceed.

## SAVE DATA TO R FILE
# At this point, you may want to save your data to an R data file
# if you want to save just the downloaded data, this would work:
save(hmp_collection, file="hmp_collection.Rda")
# if you want to save everything in your workspace
# this would work
save(list=ls(), file="workspace_backup.Rda")

## LOAD SAVED DATA
# If you have data that you save above and want to load it, you can do it this way:
load(file="hmp_collection.Rda")

# LOAD MOST CURRENT matR SCRIPTS FOR VIZUALIZATION AND STATS
# frequently, the matR package lags behind our most current capabilities
# the following code will load a number of functions that will be soon be
# part of matR - but for now are not
source_https <- function(url, ...) {
  require(RCurl)
  sapply(c(url, ...), function(u) {
    eval(parse(text = getURL(u, followlocation = TRUE, cainfo = system.file("CurlSSL", "cacert.pem", package = "RCurl"))), envir = .GlobalEnv)
  })
}

# improved normalization
source_https("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DrOppenheimer/matR-apps/master/normalize_fun.2-27-14/norm_redux.v4.r")

# function to produce raw pco
source_https("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MG-RAST/AMETHST/master/plot_pco.r")

# new function to render the raw pco with metadata (colors and legend are automatically handled)
source_https("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DrOppenheimer/matR-apps/master/plot_fun.12-10-13/pcoa/render_calculated_pcoa.dev.v11.r")

# heatmap (color bar can be used to include metadata)
source_https("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DrOppenheimer/matR-apps/master/heatmap_fun/heatmap_dendrogram.from_file.3-18-14.r")

# stats
source_https("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DrOppenheimer/matR-apps/master/stats_fun.2-27-14/matR_stats_from_files.r")

# simple script to export data as tab delimited text
export_data <- function(data_object, file_name){
  write.table(data_object, file=file_name, sep="\t", col.names = NA, row.names = TRUE, quote = FALSE, eol="\n")
}

# EXPORT DATA INTO TAB DELIMITED TEXT
# functional data
export_data(hmp_collection$ss_l3_counts,"ss_l3_counts.txt")
# taxonomic data
export_data(hmp_collection$taxa_genus_counts,"taxa_genus_counts.txt")

# NORMALIZE DATA (DESeq "blin", negative bionomial modeling to stabilize variance)
MGRAST_preprocessing("ss_l3_counts.txt")
MGRAST_preprocessing("taxa_genus_counts.txt")

# Produce raw PCoA (flat file out)
MGRAST_plot_pco("ss_l3_counts.txt.DESeq.PREPROCESSED.txt")
MGRAST_plot_pco("taxa_genus_counts.txt.DESeq.PREPROCESSED.txt")

# RENDER THE PCOAS with metadata (hmp_metadata.txt is attached) -- this will create a figure for each
# column in the metadata file
# functional PCoAs
render_pcoa.v11(
  PCoA_in="ss_l3_counts.txt.DESeq.PREPROCESSED.txt.euclidean.PCoA",
  use_all_metadata_columns=TRUE,
  figure_cex = 2,
  figure_symbol_cex=3,
  image_width_in=22,
  image_height_in=17,
  width_legend = 0.4,
  width_figure = 0.6,
  metadata_table = "hmp_metadata.txt"
)
# taxonoic PCoAs
render_pcoa.v11(
  PCoA_in="taxa_genus_counts.txt.DESeq.PREPROCESSED.txt.euclidean.PCoA",
  use_all_metadata_columns=TRUE,
  figure_cex = 2,
  figure_symbol_cex=3,
  image_width_in=22,
  image_height_in=17,
  width_legend = 0.4,
  width_figure = 0.6,
  metadata_table = "hmp_metadata.txt"
)

# system("open open *.pcoa.png") # command will open all the images on mac/linux/unix may not work on Windows

# CREATE HEATMAPS - WITH METADATA COLOR BAR

# functional (colored by body location)
heatmap_dendrogram.from_file("ss_l3_counts.txt.DESeq.PREPROCESSED.txt",
                             metadata_table="hmp_metadata.txt",
                             metadata_column="location"
                             )
# taxonomi (colored by body location)
heatmap_dendrogram.from_file("taxa_genus_counts.txt.DESeq.PREPROCESSED.txt",
                             metadata_table="hmp_metadata.txt",
                             metadata_column="location"
)
taxa_genus_counts.txt.DESeq.PREPROCESSED.txt

# STATISTICS

# Use Kruskal Wallis to find features that exhibit the most significant differences among specified groups
# groups are derived from colulmn selected from metadata -- in this case, "location"
# functional
stats_from_files(data_table="ss_l3_counts.txt.DESeq.PREPROCESSED.txt",
                 metadata_table="hmp_metadata.txt",
                 metadata_column="location",
                 stat_test="Kruskal-Wallis"
                 )
# taxonomic
stats_from_files(data_table="taxa_genus_counts.txt.DESeq.PREPROCESSED.txt",
                 metadata_table="hmp_metadata.txt",
                 metadata_column="location",
                 stat_test="Kruskal-Wallis"
                 )
# taxonomic
